title: Active catalog
prompt: Return sku, product_name for every active product (active = 1), sorted by sku.
hints: Only two columns are needed, both from products.
Active is stored as the integer 1, not as text.
SELECT ... FROM products WHERE active = ... ORDER BY ...;

title: Customer labels
prompt: Return customer_id and the customer's full name under the alias customer_label, sorted by customer_id. The column names are checked.
hints: An alias renames a column in the result, not in the table.
Use AS after the expression you want to rename.
SELECT customer_id, full_name AS ... FROM customers ORDER BY ...;

title: Distinct order statuses
prompt: Return each order status once, in a column named status, sorted alphabetically.
hints: Several orders share a status; you need each value only once.
DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.
SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders ORDER BY ...;

title: Cheap products
prompt: Return sku, unit_price_cents for products cheaper than 500 cents (any active state), cheapest first, ties by sku.
hints: Prices are integers in cents, so 500 means €5.00.
Cheaper than means strictly less than.
Sort by two keys: price first, then sku.

title: Orders needing attention
prompt: Return order_id, status for orders that are pending or cancelled, sorted by order_id.
hints: Two different status values qualify.
IN (...) is a compact way to write several OR conditions.
WHERE status IN ('...', '...')

title: Top of the org chart
prompt: Return employee_id, full_name for employees without a manager, sorted by employee_id.
hints: A missing manager is stored as NULL.
manager_id = NULL is never true. NULL needs its own operator.
WHERE manager_id IS NULL

title: Latest three orders
prompt: Return order_id, ordered_at for the three most recent orders. Newest first; break date ties by the higher order_id first.
hints: Sort first, then keep only the first rows.
Dates stored as YYYY-MM-DD text sort correctly as text.
ORDER BY ordered_at DESC, order_id DESC LIMIT 3

title: Premium shelf
prompt: Return sku, product_name, unit_price_cents for the three most expensive active products, price high to low, ties by sku.
hints: Filter to active products before ranking them.
LIMIT is applied after ORDER BY.
WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY unit_price_cents DESC, sku LIMIT 3

title: Product labels
prompt: Return one column named product_label in the form 'P01: Notebook' (sku, colon, space, product name) for every product, sorted by sku. The column name is checked.
hints: SQLite joins text with the || operator.
The separator ': ' is a text literal in single quotes.
SELECT sku || ': ' || product_name AS product_label ...

title: Catalog size
prompt: Return one row with two columns: customer_count (all customers) and product_count (all products).
hints: The two counts come from two different tables.
A subquery in the SELECT list can return a single value.
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ...) AS customer_count, (...) AS product_count;

title: Units sold
prompt: Return one row, total_quantity: the sum of quantity across all order lines (every status).
hints: Order lines live in order_items.
An aggregate without GROUP BY returns one row.
SELECT SUM(...) AS total_quantity FROM order_items;

title: Active price range
prompt: Return one row with min_price and max_price, the lowest and highest unit_price_cents among active products.
hints: Two aggregates can share one SELECT.
The filter runs before the aggregates.
SELECT MIN(...), MAX(...) FROM products WHERE active = 1;

title: Orders by status
prompt: Return status, order_count for each order status, sorted by status.
hints: One output row per status value.
GROUP BY creates the groups; COUNT(*) counts rows in each.
SELECT status, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY status ORDER BY status;

title: Repeat customers
prompt: Return customer_id, order_count for customers with more than one order (any status), sorted by customer_id.
hints: Count orders per customer first, then filter the groups.
WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.
GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

title: Revenue by payment method
prompt: Return method, paid_cents (sum of amount_cents) for each payment method that has payments, sorted by method.
hints: Payments already store the amount actually received.
Group by the method column.
SELECT method, SUM(amount_cents) ... GROUP BY method ...

title: Products with categories
prompt: Return sku, product_name, category_name for every product, sorted by sku.
hints: category_name lives in categories; products hold category_id.
Join on the shared key, and use table aliases to keep it short.
FROM products p JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id

title: Who placed each order
prompt: Return order_id, full_name, ordered_at for every order, sorted by order_id.
hints: Every order references exactly one customer.
An inner join is enough because the foreign key is NOT NULL.
FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

title: Employees and managers
prompt: Return employee (the employee's name) and manager (the manager's name, NULL when there is none) for every employee, sorted by employee_id.
hints: The manager is also a row in employees: join the table to itself.
An inner join would drop employees with no manager.
FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id

title: Never ordered
prompt: Return sku, product_name for products that never appear in any order line, sorted by sku. (The course dataset has none; the edge fixture has one.)
hints: Look for products with no matching order line.
After a LEFT JOIN, unmatched rows have NULL in every right-hand column.
LEFT JOIN order_items i ON ... WHERE i.product_id IS NULL

title: Paid order summary
prompt: For paid orders only, return order_id, line_count (number of order lines) and total_cents (sum of quantity × unit_price_cents), sorted by order_id.
hints: Combine a join, a filter and a grouping.
Multiply inside SUM, per line, using the price stored on the line.
JOIN order_items ... WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.order_id
